scope: Reproducible release inputs and classified two-build artifact comparison

release_inputs.source_identity: revision, clean state, tracked-file count and content digest
release_inputs.toolchain_identity: compiler, linker, librarian, manifest tool and resource compiler executable SHA-256 values
release_inputs.dependency_identity: cgltf revision and files, Slang version and per-platform archive hashes, GLFW tag and OptiX revision
release_inputs.configuration_identity: normalized CMake preset, override arguments and selected cache options

verification.check: python tools/check_release_reproducibility.py --preset sdk-ci --generator 'Visual Studio 18 2026' --architecture x64 --output out/release-repro/f6-04-6f821a5 --config Release --jobs 2
verification.result: PASS: two isolated clean configure/build/install runs, equivalent recorded inputs, matching artifact sets and zero required workstation-path hits
PASS: 39/39 tests, including the release reproducibility classifier suite

continuous_integration.coverage: Linux, Apple Silicon macOS and Windows each perform two clean sdk-ci builds and retain both manifests, the comparison report and logs

limitations: Bit-identical output is not established: three PE files and two static libraries differed between the two Windows builds.
Ten build-tree test manifests differed only by their intentionally distinct build-directory paths; installed runtime metadata had zero required workstation-path hits.
The observed classifications apply to this exact source, host, toolchain and input tuple; they do not assert cross-host or cross-toolchain reproducibility.
